newsitem.title: USA: Morgan sees DRAM market strong in coming months.
newsitem.headline: Morgan sees DRAM market strong in coming months.

text.p: The market for dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips will remain strong for the next two months then begin to fall late in the year, Morgan Stanley semiconductor analyst John Marren told Reuters on Tuesday.
"The DRAM market continues to be strong on a surge in orders from personal computer companies, and spot market pricing will be firm to up in coming months," he said.

Spot prices for 16 megabit DRAM chips, the most popular configuration, have risen to $10 from $8 in early August. The increase benefits all producers, including Micron Technology Inc and Texas Instruments Inc, he said.
"I think (the market) will be flat to up for the next two months and then trend down late in the year and in the beginning of '97," Marren said.
"I believe the DRAM market will be oversupplied for 1997."
